answers.reply: Cool roofs, your scenario of the Heat 2026 project, comes into this dataflow with its saved results when you drag its card in: open Scenario, Browse all (the Scenario Catalog), find Cool roofs under Heat 2026, and drag its card onto this canvas. It is not in this dataflow until you do, so I rebuilt nothing: no node, plan or code stands in for it.

answers.reply: The footprints are not in your Data Catalog yet, so no node can load them now. First they come into the Data Catalog as a dataset: download them from the City of Chicago's data portal through the Discovery Catalog, where the Dataset Finder finds the portal's building footprints and proposes the download for you to approve. Once the download lands, a node loads the dataset by its Data Catalog id, curio_load_data("<its id>"). I wrote no URL, file name or dataset id from memory, and no loader yet.

answers.source: utk_curio/backend/tests/test_agents/test_source_grounding.py::TestConnectionKeys (curio_secret("<name>") reads a key saved for node code, a Node code key, by its name and host: test_secret_calls_and_hosts and test_known_name_is_a_grounded_ref_with_its_label; a key pasted into code is refused naming curio_secret("<name>"): test_a_pasted_key_is_refused_and_the_route_named); utk_curio/backend/tests/test_agents/test_editors_drive_agents.py (the Node code keys an account saves)
answers.reply: Save the key in API Settings as a Node code key: give it a name of your choice, such as openweather, and the host of OpenWeather's API it is for. Node code then reads it only by that name, as api_key = curio_secret("openweather"), with the name you saved it under; the key itself is never written in the code, and you need not paste it here.
